texts.full_text: unimportant or false ones. Without a considerable reduction in false positives, there is little hope in providing sufficiently automated resolutions. False alarms drain resources and contribute to cognitive overload among analysts, whose time is limited and expensive. In addition, large numbers of network probes threaten to drown out significant events that require analyst attention and immediate response. Due to lack of automated responses, accurate sensors and personnel, the time required to recognize, diagnose, and act upon events in the commercial sector is in the range of days and hours. Host-based and network-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) may identify unauthorized, illicit, and anomalous behavior based on agents placed on hosts or upon network traffic. Logs from hosts, servers, firewalls and other devices may also provide an indication of unapproved and irregular activities within the network and on individual devices. Security information and event management technology has been developed and adopted by sectors in the commercial world that supports threat detection through real-time collection and analysis of security events from a wide variety of sensors and events. Improvements in IDS and SIEM technology may gradually reduce false alarm rates, but these systems cannot take overall mission needs and priorities into account. What is needed is a system/mission model that maps high-level concerns to potential low-level vulnerabilities, compromises, or indications of suspicious activity. For enterprise-scale systems, such models can become very complex; a machine-readable model is needed that can perform automated calculations of various metrics (impact, potential for loss of life, remediation cost, etc.). Such a model is also requisite for any type of automated response: it is only by assessing larger impacts that an automated system can make necessary changes without disrupting essential services. This compromises product efficacy and safety, as dissolved components may contaminate adjacent units or render them ineffective. Such vulnerabilities highlight the need for packaging solutions that balance solubility with storage stability. Rupturing of articles can be messy and inconvenient for the consumer and can cause contamination of neighbouring articles. Related to this is the tendency for neighbouring pouches to stick to one another. This results in further requirements for the consumer to handle the neighbouring pouches in order to separate them before use. Age was the strongest predictor of CAC, with the prevalence of CAC increasing with increasing age. Sex was also significantly associated with CAC, with women having a higher prevalence of CAC than men. The prevalence of CAC was higher in individuals with a family history of coronary artery disease, medical conditions, and a history of smoking. The prevalence of CAC was also higher in individuals with a higher body mass index and a history of hypertension. The geographic distribution of CAC was also analyzed, with a higher prevalence of CAC in zip codes with higher poverty rates and lower levels of education.
